clue.text: Opposed to bread lacking key element

indicators.note: a word that is lacking something has had that item taken out of it

blocks.note: anti means against or opposed to
bread is slang for cash
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone against bread is cutting out a key ingredient from their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, and key is a musical key, so the letter E is the one dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a metallic chemical element with the symbol Sb.

clue.text: Void filled by a plant

indicators.note: one word is filled with another, holding it inside

blocks.note: to void a contract is to annul it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An empty space has been filled with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Void looks like a noun meaning gap, but it is the verb meaning cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a plant that completes its life cycle within a single year.

clue.text: New co-writer upset old news reporter

indicators.note: upset means knocked about, so the letters fall into another order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A co-writer has angered a veteran journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: New is just the letter N added to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who called out public announcements in the streets before newspapers.

clue.text: One who might be best to hide revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, out of sight

blocks.note: a best mate is a closest friend
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A friend hides a weapon belonging to a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Best mate is everyday British for closest friend; Che is the standard crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used as a tool and as a weapon.

clue.text: Vote against eating toast crusts? That's smart!

indicators.note: the crusts of a slice are its edges, the first and last letters
eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: nay is a vote against
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone votes against eating toast crusts and is praised for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neatly dressed or stylish, like smart in its fashion sense.

clue.text: Sandwich, for example, set me back around £25!

indicators.note: set means placed, so one piece is set around the other piece
set back means read the little word in the opposite direction
around says one piece is wrapped about the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A sandwich at £25 sounds like an outrageous lunch bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The sandwich is named after the Earl of Sandwich, which makes the word a namesake term; the capital S hides this.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a person whose name is given to something, as the Earl of Sandwich was to the snack.

clue.text: Listen to this marine group start fishing

blocks.note: a pod is a group of whales or dolphins
to cast is to throw out a line when fishing

explanation.surface: An invitation to hear a group of sea creatures beginning to fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: something one listens to.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is an audio programme downloaded and played, something made to be heard.

clue.text: One supporter upset about a canteen where you serve yourself?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down so they read backwards
about puts one piece around another piece

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a fan supports a team
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-service canteen has upset one of its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI runs canteens and shops for the British armed forces; serving yourself here means serving in the forces, not self-service.
explanation.definitionFit: The NAAFI provides canteens for British service personnel, those who serve their country.

clue.text: Way to evaluate chair

blocks.note: a mode is a way of doing something
to rate is to assess

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to judge a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Chair is a verb here, as in chairing a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate a debate is to preside over it, which is what chairing it means.

clue.text: Campaign funds western, with most knowing to support it

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits underneath the one before

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
arch means knowing or sly, and this is its superlative

explanation.surface: A western-themed campaign is funded by the shrewdest backers.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is money reserved for a campaign, especially a political one.

clue.text: Try and scale down Barking police headquarters

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

blocks.note: the fifteen letters used for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to downsize a police HQ in Barking, an area of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a real London district, so it reads as a place name rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: New Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Researcher yet to cover outdoor sport

indicators.note: the outer words cover, or conceal, the solution inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A researcher has not yet written about some open-air sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Archery, shooting with bow and arrow at targets, is usually practised outdoors.

clue.text: Somehow alive inside box of computer keyboard

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way
the box of a word is its outside edge, its first and last letters
inside places one piece within the other

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A keyboard has somehow come back to life inside a computer case.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is a keyboard instrument, or the keyboard of one, such as a harpsichord or piano.

clue.text: Discount event with beer cans at the front

indicators.note: this phrase places one piece before the other piece in the line

blocks.note: to can someone is to sack or dismiss them
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A sale where the cans of beer are displayed at the front of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Cans looks like a noun for beer tins, but it is the verb meaning dismisses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire sale is a sale of goods at heavily reduced prices, originally of fire-damaged stock.

clue.text: Shows pilot and flight attendants the propeller

blocks.note: to air something is to show or broadcast it
the people working on an aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone shows the pilot and cabin staff the plane's propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: An airscrew is an aircraft propeller, an older British term.

clue.text: Firm on leaving later today

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are removed from the larger word

blocks.note: taken as written
the evening of today

explanation.surface: A firm is deciding about being on leave later today.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and tight are synonyms for something securely fixed or held.

clue.text: Rudely ignore old person on a boat

indicators.note: rudely suggests roughness, so the letters are roughly jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rudely ignores an elderly passenger on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola, the flat-bottomed boat of Venice's canals.

clue.text: Pieces bound for store

blocks.note: pawns are chess pieces
a hop is a little jump or bound

explanation.surface: Goods that are packed and bound for a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound looks like heading for, but it is a noun meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnshop is a store that lends money against items left as security.

clue.text: Pointer — remove tip from vegetable

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, which is to be cut away

blocks.note: a marrow is a large British squash

explanation.surface: Advice on preparing a vegetable: cut the tip off first.
explanation.walkthrough: A marrow is an oversized courgette, a common British vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign or symbol used to point the way.

clue.text: Breeding facility problem is consuming me

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a worry is a problem
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a problem with a breeding farm is eating them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wormery is a container in which worms are kept and bred, often for composting.

clue.text: Turning in circle to embrace ritual from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means going right to left
one piece hugs the other piece, holding it inside

blocks.note: a ring is a circle
a rite is a ritual

explanation.surface: Dancers turning in a circle to perform an eastern ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning looks like rotation, but turning in is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring means going to bed for the night, which is what turning in means.

clue.text: Hold back repeated melody

blocks.note: first meaning: to stop oneself doing something
second meaning: the chorus that recurs in a song

explanation.surface: Someone resisting the urge to hum a catchy tune again.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for abstaining and a noun for a recurring chorus in music.

clue.text: Like some lattes from pub in island that closes early

indicators.note: closing early means stopping before the final letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Skye is a Scottish island
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Coffees from a pub on an island where everything shuts early.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Skye is off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinny latte is made with skimmed milk, so skinny describes some lattes.

clue.text: Digital nomad's first rum mixed with ice

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word before
mixed suggests the letters are stirred together into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter
letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A digital nomad mixes a rum on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Digital nomad is a set phrase for a remote worker, which hides that Digital alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital and numeric both describe data expressed in numbers or digits.

clue.text: Study upset dog? Let me think…

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down so they read backwards

blocks.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
the hesitation noise made while thinking

explanation.surface: Someone pondering what to study about a distressed dog.
explanation.walkthrough: To mug up is British slang for cramming for an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is to study a subject intensively, especially before a test.

clue.text: County's bad mood inspiring poorly bowled over

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked upside down, so it is read backwards
inspiring means breathing in, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: a sulk is a fit of bad mood
feeling off means feeling poorly

explanation.surface: A cricket county sulks after a bowler is poorly and gets knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is an English county on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is one of the counties of eastern England.

clue.text: Exercise spot that's unlawfully occupied

blocks.note: first meaning: a knees-bend exercise
second meaning: a building lived in without the owner's permission

explanation.surface: A place to work out that has been taken over illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gym movement of bending the knees and a property taken over by people without legal right.

clue.text: Trainee pilots may need this type of tuition?

definitions.text: Trainee pilots may need this type of tuition?

blocks.clueFragment: Trainee pilots may need this type of tuition?
blocks.note: surface reading: the kind of teaching student aviators require, learning to fly up in the sky
setter's reading: university-level study, which is schooling beyond the secondary level

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: pilots fly high, so their lessons happen at altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means university and college study, and here also lessons taken aloft in a plane.

clue.text: Old man with chopped potato and fruit

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: papa is an old-fashioned word for father
a yam is a starchy tuber, and the sweet potato is called a yam in America

explanation.surface: Father is served chopped potatoes with fruit on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya is a tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Fools back dull American swimmer

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: nits is British slang for idiots
the American spelling of grey, meaning dull

explanation.surface: Fools turning their backs on a dull American swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish, so a creature that swims in the sea.
